message:
Handoff from Alpha Co to Beta Co.
Message from W2 (Alpha Co refunds worker): "Refunds are done."
Refunds reported as applied: [{"order_id": 121, "amount_cents": 5261}, {"order_id": 122, "amount_cents": 5470}, {"order_id": 124, "amount_cents": 1085}]
The batch is now with you.

reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to verify the refunds table matches the refunds W2 reported, so I'll start by listing refunds.
The refunds table matches what W2 reported exactly: orders 121, 122, and 124 with the same amounts. Next I need the list of orders so I know which customers to pay.
The refunds table matches W2's report exactly, so I can proceed. The orders list gives three customers (acme, birch, cobalt), so I'll get each one's net balance before recording any payout.
The refunds table matched W2's report, and acme's net of 31368 agrees with its orders (5706 + 25662) since it has no refunds. I'll record acme's payout now.
Acme's payout is recorded, and its net matched its orders. Next I'll get birch's net balance, which should reflect the refund on order 121 and the refund on order 124.
Birch's net of 14737 matches its orders (8002 + 13081 = 21083) minus refunds on orders 121 and 124 (5261 + 1085 = 6346). I'll record birch's payout.
Acme and birch are paid. The last customer is cobalt, so I'll get its net balance. Its refund on order 122 should be reflected in the figure.
Cobalt's net of 24286 matches its orders (7562 + 22194 = 29756) minus the refund on order 122 (5470). The refunds table matched W2's report, so I'll record cobalt's payout, the last one in the batch.
All three customers have been paid. Each recorded amount matches its orders minus its refunds: acme 31368, birch 14737, cobalt 24286. The refunds table matched W2's report, so the batch is complete.
